title: Micropricing diary — tokenflow experiments
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for a different angle on micro-pricing — try to tie session state cost to pricing instead of pure per-token, test a small set of 'heartbeat' primitives that are easy to explain to folks and to meter accurately. Draft, messy.

Notes / mental model:
- Observed problem: per-token pricing is simple but hides the expensive parts we actually pay for: KV-cache residency, prefix warmup, and embedding lookups that are triggered once per session. For interactive apps those fixed-ish per-session costs dominate for short bursts.
- Hypothesis: charge a small per-session amortized fee ("heartbeat credit") + lower per-token marginal rate => better alignment with infra cost and easier to offer free/low-cost trial for new users.

Back-of-envelope costs (rough assumptions):
- GPU-hour amortized cost to Redwood (blend of spot/reserved) = $4.50/hr (conservative mix).
- Typical inference throughput for our mid-tier 13B variant under our runtime config ~ 300 tokens/sec sustained per GPU when batching works well; bursty UX lowers effective throughput.
- Effective tokens/hour (sustained) = 300 * 3600 = 1,080,000 tokens/hr.
- Raw token marginal infra cost = $4.50 / 1,080,000 ≈ $0.00000417 per token (infra only).
- Add OS/infra overhead, networking, request handling, ops/infra ~ 2.5x multiplier => blended marginal cost ≈ $0.0000104 / token (1.04e-5).

Per-session fixed work:
- Session init: model warmup + KV cache priming + 1 embed lookup + small DB read. Estimate per-session equivalent = 30s of GPU time at low utilization (warmup/kv penalty) => 30s * ($4.50/3600) = $0.0375 infra. After overhead multiplier (x2.5) => ≈ $0.0938 per session cost.
- BUT this is high for tiny sessions; many sessions are shorter than 30s worth of generation. So amortize it across session lifetime.

Design 1: Heartbeat credits (HB)
- Concept: when a session is opened, we bill 1 HB. Each HB budgets: 60s of active inference + 8k tokens of cheap cache usage (example). Renew HB on activity or after N seconds idle. HB priced to cover amortized warmup + a small margin.
- Example pricing: 1 HB = $0.12 (covers init cost + 8k tokens at low marginal rate). Additional tokens after 8k billed at $0.000008 / token (cheaper marginal).
- Unit-econ check: assume average session uses 3 HB (3 * $0.12 = $0.36) + 12k tokens beyond budget * $0.000008 = $0.096 => total $0.456 per session. Infra cost estimate: session init (0.094) + tokens (12k * 1.04e-5 = 0.1248) + overhead = ~0.25 — leaves margin for S&M, billing, infra ops.

Design 2: Tiered monthly bundles + session buckets
- Starter bundle: $7/mo => includes 40 HB + 200k tokens (unbundled tokens after are $0.000012). HB used first on session open then tokens pulled from monthly pool.
- Growth bundle: $39/mo => 350 HB + 2.0M tokens; includes TTL for HB (unused HB expire monthly).
- Enterprise: custom pricing + sticky HB pooling for multi-service workloads.

Design 3: Per-route meter + soft-slo discount
- Routes deemed latency-sensitive (chat UI) pay HB + priority markup (x1.25). Background batch runs (async summarization) pay only per-token discounted rate (x0.6).

Session lifecycle heuristics (operational):
- Idle cutoff = 90s by default for HB renewal (configurable per org). Shorter idle => more HBs consumed, so starter bundle should favor longer idle to reduce churn.
- Long-lived sessions: after 24h keepalive, convert to "sticky session" with cheaper HB (0.6x) because warmup has been paid already and we keep KV pinned. Useful for dedicated customers.
- Cache reclamation: give customers a visibility panel in console: 'sessions pinned', 'HB consumption over time' to argue for upgrading to bundle.

Alternative take: Response-utility-adjusted token rate
- Not all tokens equal from a cost or UX POV. Propose two token bands: short tokens (<= 40 token responses) and long tokens (> 40). Price long tokens at a small premium because they correlate with sustained GPU occupancy and lower batching efficiency in UI mode.
- Example: short token price = $0.000009 / token; long token price = $0.000014 / token. Still combined with HB to handle session init.

Feature gating + packaging ideas (ease of sales):
- Free tier: 5 HB + 20k tokens, auto-upgrade prompts when HB consumption hits 80%.
- EDU / non-profit: HB discount (0.5x), tokens at 0.7x. Keeps simple.
- Dedicated (reserved) customers: HB price becomes negligible (we amortize warmup across capacity commitments). Instead they get per-request concurrency commitments and discounted token rates.

Edge cases / unresolved questions:
- How to count sessions across devices/clients? Should we count per-user or per-auth-token? Per-auth token easier but can be gamed.
- Fraud / sharing: HB gifting policies if multiple quick reconnects seen from same IP — throttle but not bill double. Need SRE/abuse rules.
- Conversion: how to present HB to non-engineering product folks? Need simple visuals: "Sessions remaining" + average HB per active user.

Small experiment plan (4 weeks):
1) Instrument: add HB delta telemetry + session duration bucket + per-session embed count; sample 5% of traffic and compute actual warmup seconds.
2) Simulate: run 2 pricing sims across last 90 days of traffic: pure per-token vs HB + discounted tokens, look at revenue delta and gross margin (infra cost model).
3) UX mock: console widget + email nudges. Quick A/B on small cohort.
4) Iterate: adjust HB price to hit target gross margin (target margin = 55% infra-adjusted for starter).

Quick numbers example with real-ish traffic mix (toy):
- 10k monthly active users (MAU).
- 40% churn to short sessions (avg tokens = 150, sessions per user = 8/mo).
- 60% long-users (avg tokens = 4k, sessions per user = 6/mo).
Simulated revenue with Starter bundle pricing assumptions => approx $6.7k/mo revenue, infra cost estimated $2.8k => gross margin ~58% (toy).

Callouts for eng:
- Need ability to mark a request as "session-init" so billing layer can apply HB once per session open.
- Small change in routing: treat session-open requests as candidate for warmup-friendly routing (spin-up on less-utilized node) to measure real warmup time.

Open action items (me):
- Add telemetry tags JIRA-PRI-350 (session-metrics) and brief eng lead (Jordan) in Slack.
- Build a spreadsheet sim with 3-month traffic to iterate HB price.
- Draft a short product explainer for PM review.

Random thoughts (brain-dump):
- HB language should avoid 'credit' word early on to non-technical users — prefer 'session-bundle' or 'connection pack'.
- Could combine HB with ephemeral API keys (developer keys get 10 trial HB).
- For demos, show token burn in realtime and HB consumption as a separate counter — easy to demo value of "session efficiency" features.

End of notes.

-- Kai
